newsitem.title: EL SALVADOR: El Salvador dollar repatriations rise Jan-April.
newsitem.headline: El Salvador dollar repatriations rise Jan-April.

text.p: Salvadoran residents in the United States increased dollar repatriations by 4.6 percent in the first four months of the year compared to the same period a year earlier, the central bank said Friday.
Dollar savings sent to El Salvador increased $15.7 million to $354.5 million from $338.8 million despite the fear that dollar incomes would be reduced because of changes in U.S. immigration law.
Those fears mushroomed because in the first three months of the year foreign exchange earnings from Salvadorans sending money back to their families dipped by $3 million, the central bank said.

Repatriated January-March earnings dropped to $251.2 million from $254.2 million in the same period a year earlier. Last year, the source of income for the Central American nation reached $1.0865 billion.
